DocFlow · visual walkthrough

Cold workspace to
documents processing.

Your workspace is empty right now: no app, no warehouse, no schema, no agents. Follow these six steps and you will be watching documents move through Agent Bricks in about fifteen minutes.

6 steps0 or 1 commands 3 buttons to pressrun takes ~2 min
1

Install it

4 to 6 min

Pick whichever suits the workspace you are in. Both end in the same place.

A · From Git, no command line at all. Best in a customer workspace, or on any machine without the Databricks CLI.

  1. In the Databricks workspace: Workspace, Create, Git folder, paste the URL below, Create. It needs no credentials.
  2. Open setup_databricks.py inside the clone and press Run all.
repo url, paste into the git folder dialog
https://github.com/jvangordon/docflow

The notebook runs as you, which is what makes this work: it creates the app, deploys the code straight out of the Git folder, then grants the app the two rights it needs to set the workspace up for itself. It finishes by printing a link to the app.

To update later: press Pull in the Git folder, then run the notebook again.

B · One command, if you have the CLI.

paste into terminal
git clone https://github.com/jvangordon/docflow && cd docflow && python3 install.py

Does exactly the same three things, and prints the app URL when it finishes.

2

Open it

1 min

Open your app URL. You land on Start. The left column is the three things you do, numbered. The right column is what the app builds for you the moment you press go.

What you are looking at

Nothing on the right is homework. The classifier, the Knowledge Assistant, extraction and the Genie space are all built for you during the run, and the checks list says so under "Built for you at go".

3

Press one button

1 min

The app tells you what the workspace is missing in plain language, and offers to fix all of it at once.

Set up this workspaceCreates everything the demo needs About 45 seconds. Each piece reports for itself underneath, so if one fails you know which.
What it just made

A 2X-Small serverless warehouse that stops itself after 10 idle minutes, a schema for the tables and Genie space, and a volume with folders for documents. When it finishes the card turns green and says the workspace is ready.

Curious what it checked? Open All 10 checks for the full list. Rows that need compute say "verified at go" instead of pretending to pass, and the two agent rows sit under "Built for you at go" with nothing for you to do.

4

Two answers

30 sec

Left side. These drive everything the run generates.

FieldWhat it changes
Customer nameAppears on every page and inside every generated document
IndustryThe vocabulary, the suggested questions, and the titles of both operations pages
Catalog and schemaWhere the tables, Genie space and run state live
DocumentsLeave as generate everything, or point at a volume of the customer's own PDFs
Try something other than Manufacturing

Type any industry you like — the chips just fill the box. Insurance gives you "Loss Run Review" and vocabulary like subrogation. Logistics gives you "Freight Claims Recovery Desk". It is the most convincing thirty seconds of the demo and it costs nothing to try.

There is no save button. Every field saves itself as you type, so a reload never loses your entries. Go enables the moment both fields are filled.

5

Press Go, then give the cue

~2 min

Go stages everything and stops: workspace, model, documents written, agents deployed — and nothing processed. The log ends on Staged, waiting for you.

Now open Flow, get the room looking at the empty lanes, and press.

AtWhat happens
~8sSchema, volume and tables confirmed
~12sLanguage model probed until one answers — the log names the model this run will use
~20sCompany research, on that same model
~40sDocuments generated, watermarked, into their own folder
~45sKnowledge Assistant created · indexing continues in the background and never blocks the run
~52sStaged. Everything waits for your cue
you pressProcess documents — parse, classify, route, extract, audit, secure, live on the lanes
~2 min laterGenie space over the extracted tables, an honest assistant status, then Ready

This is the screen to show a customer.

6

The payoff

3 min

Three screens carry the story once the run is done.

Ask — the suggestions under the box are written for your industry and are guaranteed answerable from the data this run produced.

Claims and Suppliers are the two operations screens. Built lists everything the run created with per section timings.

✓

Stand it down

10 sec

Nothing bills while idle. The warehouse stops itself after 10 minutes and Databricks stops the app 24 hours after deploy. To stop the app immediately:

paste into terminal
databricks apps stop docflow

To wipe everything and start over — the app, the assistant, the schema and every document — open reset_databricks.py in the Git folder and press Run all. It removes things in the order that works and prints what it did.

If a fix button fails

The message leads with what to do about it, and Databricks' own wording sits behind a "what Databricks reported" disclosure. Usually it means step 3 was skipped or did not finish.

Every screenshot on this page is a real capture of the app running against a Databricks workspace. Nothing is mocked up.
